headline: Non-cash impairment swamps GAAP results as outlook improves
summary_short: Kraft Heinz posted a GAAP net loss of $5.46B ($(4.60) diluted EPS) in Q2 FY2026 on $7.35B of non-cash impairment charges, while net sales of $6.26B fell 1.4% y/y and Adjusted EPS of $0.56 declined 18.8% y/y; the company raised its full-year Organic Net Sales and Adjusted EPS outlook.
summary_long: GAAP operating loss of $6.4B and net loss of $5.46B (diluted EPS $(4.60)) were driven almost entirely by $7.35B of non-cash goodwill/intangible impairment, down from $9.27B a year earlier. Adjusted Operating Income fell 18.4% y/y to $1.04B on higher advertising, unfavorable volume/mix, input-cost inflation, and higher variable compensation, partly offset by pricing and efficiency gains. Net sales fell 1.4% y/y (Organic -1.3%) as 1.3pp of price was outweighed by a 2.6pp volume/mix decline, mainly in meats/spoonables and Easter-timing shifts. Cash fell to $2.42B q/q on debt repayment and dividends. Management raised FY2026 Organic Net Sales guidance to (0.5)%-(2.0)% and Adjusted EPS guidance to $2.03-$2.09, while lowering Constant-Currency Adjusted Operating Income guidance to (16)%-(18)%, reflecting $700M of incremental brand investment.

Diluted EPS q/q delta is expressed as a dollar change, not a percentage, because the prior quarter (FY2026 Q1, $0.67) was profitable while Q2 was a loss, making a percentage change meaningless.

drivers.explanation: Price gains of 1.3pp across all segments were outweighed by a 2.6pp volume/mix decline, driven by lower meats and spoonables volumes and an Easter-timing shift (~100bp), partly offset by an inventory pull-forward benefit (~80bp).
Improvement vs. prior year is due to non-cash impairment losses being $1.9B lower than the year-ago quarter ($7.35B vs $9.27B), not an improvement in underlying operations.
Loss narrowed y/y for the same reason as operating income — a smaller non-cash impairment charge than the year-ago quarter.
Swing from a $0.67 profit in Q1 FY2026 to a $(4.60) loss in Q2 is explained by the quarter's $7.35B impairment charge, which Q1 did not carry.
Cash declined q/q on $2.98B of long-term debt repayments and continued dividend payments, partially offset by operating cash flow and new debt issuance.

Management said results exceeded expectations across U.S. Retail, Global Away From Home, and Emerging Markets, raised the Organic Net Sales outlook, and is adding $100M of incremental brand investment (to ~$700M) for 2026.
